standard_prerequisites.name: A pseudo-coherent complex whose cohomology in the relevant degrees is finite can be cut in two at a degree after localizing at a suitable element, producing a direct sum decomposition of the truncations
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: invoked at proof lines 19852-19856 and again at proof lines 19857-19862
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies both splittings: the first separates the truncation above the degree from the rest, the second separates the cohomology module in that degree.

core_obligations: Apply the cutting statement to K at the degree i to obtain the first condition, namely that the truncation above i becomes perfect with tor amplitude bounded below, together with a splitting of K into the truncations below and above that degree (proof lines 19852-19856).

Apply the same statement once more to the truncation below the degree in question, choosing the localizing element suitably, to split that truncation into the part below i minus one and the cohomology module placed in degree i (proof lines 19857-19861).

Read off that the cohomology module becomes flat and perfect over the localization, hence a finite free module, and combine the two splittings into the asserted canonical direct sum decomposition (proof lines 19862-19864).
proof_roadmap: Cut K at the degree in question to get the perfect truncation and the first splitting (proof lines 19852-19856).
Cut the lower truncation again with a suitably chosen element to isolate the cohomology module (proof lines 19857-19861).
Identify that module as finite free and assemble the two splittings (proof lines 19862-19864).
